title: Stinginess and envy
intro: Two bad qualities that often come together – and how a believer protects themselves from them.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says that Shaytan scares you with poverty and pushes you to be stingy, while Allah promises you His forgiveness and His reward. Allah is All-Generous and All-Knowing. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:268)</small>

Stinginess is one of the worst human qualities, and a stingy person is among the most disliked. Stinginess can show in many parts of life, but most of all it means being stingy with wealth: keeping it all for yourself, holding it back from people around you – often even from those closest to you, whom you must feed and look after. Stinginess comes from selfishness and from the fear of becoming poor.

items: not trusting what Allah (SWT) has said,
not following what the Prophet (SAW) recommended,
not believing in Allah’s decree about provision (rizq),
holding back kindness from your own family,
not giving sadaqah from your wealth,
not spending wealth on good causes,
living in fear of becoming poor,
wealth getting smaller, and its barakah (blessing) disappearing.

learn.html: On the Day of Judgement we will have to answer for our wealth: how we earned it and how we spent it. The Prophet (SAW) said: “The feet of the servant of Allah will not move on the Day of Judgement until he is asked about his life – how he used it; about his knowledge – what he did with it; about his wealth – how he earned it and how he spent it; and about his body – what he used it for.” (Tirmidhi)

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “…The stingy person is far from Allah, far from people, far from Jannah and close to Jahannam. An ignorant person who is generous is dearer to Allah than a stingy worshipper.” (Tirmidhi)
Stinginess and envy are linked by cause and effect: a stingy person very often becomes envious, and an envious person becomes stingy.

Envy (hasad) is a bad quality that shows as a negative feeling towards someone who has something the envious person does not have. There are different kinds of envy: from badness in the soul, to mild hostility, all the way to open aggression – when the envious person sees good and happiness leave the other person.

Envy is a dangerous illness, and it has been known since Allah created Adam (AS) – Shaytan, who is cursed, envied him. Envy is found in every time, also in ours, and every sincere believer must guard against it. It destroys trust between people, breaks their communication and leads to other big sins. Sadly, many people are glad when someone else is unhappy, and sad when a Muslim succeeds or gets a good position or wealth.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says about the enemies of the believers: when something good happens to you, it upsets them, and when something bad happens to you, they are glad. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all. Allah knows well what they do. <small>(Qur’an, Ali ‘Imran 3:120)</small>

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: In a beautiful picture, the Prophet (SAW) showed how dangerous envy is: “Beware of envy, for envy eats up good deeds just as fire eats up wood.” (Abu Dawud)
People become envious because of hatred, hostility, arrogance, fear of losing their position, hidden stinginess and bad character.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “There is no envy except in two cases: a person whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it on the path of truth, and a person whom Allah has given wisdom and who judges by it and teaches it to others.” (Bukhari)
This kind of “envy” is not a bad quality. It is simply the wish that we too could have wealth to spend on things that please Allah (SWT) – or knowledge to share.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Every Muslim must seek refuge with Allah (SWT) from bad qualities, and stinginess and envy are among them. A believer wishes for good; a hypocrite envies.

items.text: “I won’t share my snacks, I might run out.”
“I won’t give any sadaqah this Ramadan.”
“I hope she loses her new bike.”
“I’m upset that he won the prize.”
“I wish I knew the Qur’an like her, so I could teach it too.”
“I wish I had money like him, so I could help the poor.”
